answer.effective_date: July 1, 2026 (current version; the document is reissued periodically — e.g., a prior version was revised October 1, 2025)
criteria_quotes: "Surgery of the ankle is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances. For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP: Procedures: Arthrodesis, Ankle (Talotibial Joint); Arthroscopy, Surgical, Ankle; Arthrotomy, Ankle; Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle. Click here to view the InterQual® criteria." (Coverage Rationale section, applicable to CPT 27702 under 'Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle')

From UHCprovider.com's Commercial policy terms and conditions page: "UnitedHealthcare may use tools developed by third parties, such as the InterQual® criteria, to assist us in administering health benefits. ... The InterQual® criteria are proprietary to Optum and are not published on this website."
answer.appeal_deadline: The notice states the appeal must be received within 180 days of the notice date (2026-08-20), i.e., by 2027-02-16.
answer.submission_route: The notice itself does not print a mailing address, fax number, or portal link — only the deadline and reference number (POC-55381BDBC3-44861). Based on UnitedHealthcare's standard channels for member appeals, submission is normally made either (a) online through the member portal (myuhc.com, using the 'Member Service Request Form'), (b) by phone using the number on the back of the member ID card, or (c) in writing to the appeals address printed on the Explanation of Benefits/Evidence of Coverage or member ID card. A commonly used UnitedHealthcare member appeals mailing address is UnitedHealthcare Member Inquiry/Appeals, P.O. Box 30432, Salt Lake City, UT 84130-0432, but this varies by specific plan/product and is not confirmed as correct for this member's exact plan.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The policy's 'Coverage Rationale' does not spell out itemized medical-necessity criteria in the public document; it instead directs reviewers to Optum's InterQual® CP: Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle criteria. UnitedHealthcare explicitly states on its provider policy site that 'InterQual® criteria are proprietary to Optum and are not published on this website.' The patient/provider should (1) call the number on the back of the member ID card and formally request, in writing, the specific InterQual criteria/clinical rationale applied to this denial (insurers are generally required to disclose the specific rule, guideline, or criterion relied upon in a denial upon request, e.g., under ERISA claims regulations and ACA internal-appeals rules), and (2) ask the ordering provider's office whether it already has InterQual access (many hospitals/orthopedic practices subscribe to InterQual and can pull the exact ankle-TJR criteria to compare against the submitted chart) to identify precisely which documentation elements (e.g., imaging severity, failed conservative treatment, functional limitation measures) were deemed 'incomplete.'
answer.notes: There is an unresolved discrepancy in the letter itself: it labels the plan 'UnitedHealthcare Community Plan (Commercial/ACA), state of Hawaii.' These are actually two different UnitedHealthcare product lines with different governing policies and different appeal timelines. I located and reviewed: (1) the UnitedHealthcare Commercial and Individual Exchange Medical Policy 'Surgery of the Ankle' (Policy Number 2026T0622O, effective 07/01/2026), which lists CPT 27702 under 'Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle' and defers entirely to Optum's InterQual® criteria (not publicly published); and (2) the Hawaii UnitedHealthcare Community Plan (QUEST Integration Medicaid) Grievances and Appeals member document, which shows a 60-calendar-day appeal deadline, not 180 days. Since the denial notice specifies a 180-day appeal deadline (consistent with ACA/Individual Exchange or ERISA commercial plan rules, not the 60-day Hawaii Medicaid Community Plan rule), I treated this as a Commercial/Individual Exchange plan and cited the corresponding Commercial policy. If the plan is in fact the Hawaii Medicaid Community Plan (QUEST), the correct policy would instead be a Hawaii-specific or generic UnitedHealthcare Community Plan 'Surgery of the Ankle' medical policy (I found a Kentucky-specific analog, CS340KY.10, but could not locate a Hawaii-specific or generic non-state Community Plan version of this exact policy), and the true appeal deadline would be 60 calendar days, not 180 — a discrepancy the patient should flag and clarify directly with the plan before relying on the 180-day date. In all versions of the ankle-surgery policy I found (Commercial, Oxford, and Kentucky Community Plan), the actual line-item medical-necessity criteria for CPT 27702 are not spelled out in the public PDF; the policy only points to Optum's proprietary InterQual® 'Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle' criteria set, which UnitedHealthcare states on its own website is not published publicly. I was not able to locate the specific mailing address/fax/portal instructions for filing the appeal for this exact plan type because the notice text provided did not include that information and it depends on which plan (Commercial/Exchange vs. Community Plan Medicaid) actually applies.
